newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar slippage weighs on options vols.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar slippage weighs on options vols.

text.p: Some intraday slippage in an otherwise range-bound dollar Thursday pressured implied volatilities for dollar/pair options, brokers said.
"They're (vols) coming down...(because) spot's going down," said one bank options broker.
"Volatility in the major currencies is a little bit lower, dollar/yen, dollar/mark, the vols are just a touch softer," added a second options broker.
"It looks like dollar/mark vols and dollar/yen vols are coming off," agreed a third broker. "We settled down in spot and people decided to sell volatility."
One-month dollar/mark had deteriorated near midday to 9.75/9.95 percent, down from Thursday's New York opening at 10.3/10.5 percent and versus 10.5/10.8 Wednesday afternoon.
One-month dollar/yen eased to 10.05/10.35 percent from 10.3/10.4 open and 10.7/11.0 late Wednesday. One-year yen dipped to 10.8/10.9 from 11.0/11.1 open.
"Sterling's being sold off as well," the third broker said.

He said one-year cable opened at 10.0/10.1 percent and some one-year, 40-delta strangles traded later at 9.9 percent. One-week sterling "traded a bunch" at 9.75 percent early and then dipped to 9.0/9.5 percent.
Risk-reversals showed little movement Thursday but shaded slightly away from puts as vols eased, said the second broker.
"The risk-reversals, which yesterday were more skewed to currency puts, (are) a little bit lower now and the calls have more relative value," he said.
The skew for yen calls stayed well below last week's peak, but puts by midday Thursday were less bid than earlier in the session as volatility slipped, he said.
The third broker quoted the 25-delta one-month dollar/yen risk reversal at 0.3/0.5 point for yen calls versus 0.1/0.4 late Wednesday.
The one-month 25-delta mark risk reversal stood at 0.3/0.5 point but favored mark puts, compared to 0.35/0.65 quoted late Wednesday.
